_rules: 0) 保留 ** 强调、`code`、链接与表格结构，与中文侧逐块对应。
1) 官方英文引文原样保留；档案里的中文转述引文在英文侧标注 (translated)，不伪造英文原文。
2) 「未核验/官方未给」等未知语义不升级；不借翻译改事实。

axes.model_access: **The official what-is page states explicitly: Powered by Amazon Bedrock** — models are invoked through Bedrock; the models answer questions over Bedrock-augmented AWS content; includes automated abuse detection (a Bedrock-side safety mechanism). Users cannot self-select the underlying model (the official gives no model picker); BYOK does not apply — billing and accounts go through AWS.
axes.runtime: **Two form lines**: the IDE plugin (conversation, inline completion, generating new code, security vulnerability scans, language upgrades/debugging/optimization and other code transformations inside VS Code / JetBrains) and the command line (official CLI page original: "The Q CLI has become the Kiro CLI" — the CLI line has migrated to the Kiro brand). The positioning is a generative assistant for "understanding, building, extending and operating AWS applications"; AWS architecture/resources/best-practices/docs Q&A is the official main line.
axes.local_files: The IDE plugin processes code inside your local IDE (completion/generation/scanning happen within the plugin workflow). **Whether code leaves the machine to the service side is not verified one by one** (Bedrock inference being service-side is a settled fact). The Q&A surface references your AWS resource context (official framing: cited answers grounded in your AWS resources and architecture).
axes.background: **No official long-running async task surface** (no background-continuation statement verified). Agentic coding capabilities are pointed by the official to Kiro (EOL announcement original: "For capabilities similar to Amazon Q Developer IDE plugins, explore Kiro… including agentic coding, chat and MCP support").
axes.tools: Built-in IDE-plugin capabilities listed officially: code conversation, inline completion, generating new code, security scans, code transformations (Java version upgrades etc.), debugging and optimization. **MCP support sits on the Kiro side** (the EOL announcement names Kiro as having MCP support); MCP on the Amazon Q plugin side is not verified.
axes.context: Context is anchored on the AWS side: your AWS resources, architecture, documentation and support content (official what-is page framing); inside the IDE it follows the current project. **Cross-session memory: not verified to an official statement.**
axes.permissions: Accounts and billing go through AWS (IAM/account system). Approval details for the IDE plugin operating on local files are not verified one by one. Bedrock-side automated abuse detection is the officially stated safety mechanism.
axes.fit:
Good fit: heavy AWS users — architecture/resource/best-practice questions with citations, and official-signature transformation tasks in the IDE like Java upgrades and security scans.

Not a fit: wanting agentic coding's new capabilities (the official clearly points to Kiro), betting long-term on the IDE plugin line (support ends 2027-04-30, see pitfalls).

runs:
This site has not completed measured runs. The test protocol is at [protocols/coding/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/coding/_protocol.md).

**Suggested measurement** (three, each pointing at something the official readable pages do not give):

- **The plugin's actual usable window after EOL** (whether the plugin keeps updating with IDE versions before 2027-04-30)
- **The concrete boundary of what the IDE plugin uploads to the service side** (which content leaves the machine for completion/scanning)
- **Whether the China regions (GDS/NNET) have corresponding feature surfaces** (not verified)
unknowns:
- Whether the IDE plugin side supports MCP (the official names MCP support only on the Kiro side)
- Cross-session memory mechanism (not verified to an official statement)
- Details of the approval model for the plugin operating on local files (not verified one by one)
- Feature surface in the China regions (not verified)
related: Same vendor's successor line: the AWS official EOL announcement names Kiro as taking over agentic coding/chat/MCP; the Q CLI has become the Kiro CLI.
Both IDE-form comparisons: Cursor is a standalone IDE with no EOL risk; Amazon Q is a plugin inside your existing editor and already has a fixed end-of-support date.
Cross-category comparison: the Amazon Q plugin has no MCP surface (not stated officially); GitHub integration goes through its own plugin system.
